target_customer: Facebook and social network players of casual games (revenue from in-game purchases and ads), plus other social game developers as potential users of its analytics tool
problem: Social game developers needed to ship many small games quickly and to know which ones were gaining traction; Gamador built games in about a week and built its own ranking and analytics tool, Rankador, described as a PageRank for social games.
business_model: Free-to-play social games monetized by virtual goods and advertising (per YC description; revenue not reported)
product_category: Social games and social game analytics

founders.name: Dan Silberman
founders.background_notes: YC founder page describes him as a product-oriented software engineer focused on UX, data engineering and data science who has founded and worked at startups in consumer, fintech and healthcare. No employers or schools named.

exit.reason: No public statement found; the YC directory lists the company as Inactive and CB Insights labels it dead.

competitors.name: Zynga
competitors.what: Largest Facebook social game developer (FarmVille, Mafia Wars, YoVille, Zynga Poker)
competitors.traction_then: Four of the top ten Facebook games by the period coverage

competitors.name: Playdom
competitors.what: Facebook and MySpace social game developer that was acquiring smaller studios
competitors.traction_then: Social City reached over 12 million monthly users by April 2010 per later coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: Casual Facebook games built in about a week each by a two person team and a custom analytics tool; the engineering was standard web and Flash work for 2010, with no research-grade parts.

defensibility.rationale: Quick, small games are easy to clone, and the company states its edge is speed of release rather than data, network effects or technology others lacked.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large studios were consolidating small developers in 2010 (for example Playdom bought several studios), but no source shows any of them acting on Gamador.

market_need_then: Facebook social games were booming in 2009 and 2010, with large developers growing fast, but Facebook limits on app notifications in 2010 reduced viral growth for small developers.

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found no press, logo description or community mentions for Gamador; nothing shows the brand had any recognition.

outcome_analysis: Gamador was a two person Winter 2010 social game studio that shipped three games and built the Rankador analytics tool, but no coverage of its traction, any later funding, or the reason it became inactive exists in public sources, so the cause of the shutdown is not public. The only dated funding signal is a database entry around February 2010 and a tiny total, which suggests it never raised beyond the YC deal.
notes: No company website is listed on the YC page, so there was no site to fetch (dead or never listed). The $20K total comes only from CB Insights and the February 2010 date from Seedtable, so the round rests on databases and is unverified; CB Insights places HQ in Mountain View while YC says San Francisco. The Zynga and Playdom entries rely on a 2009 Adweek article about top Facebook social game developers and a search summary of 2010 coverage; their traction is not quoted. No dated source on direct competitors for week-long game development or social game analytics was found.
